program_name: Structural and Geotechnical Engineering (STReGA) — IMPORTANT CLASSIFICATION CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF. The brief records this item as "type: curriculum, curriculum_of: Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica". That is not how the University classifies it. "STReGA" is the University's own acronym for the WHOLE degree "Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica", and "Structural and Geotechnical Engineering" is simply the official English name of that same degree — not the name of a track inside a differently-named Italian programme. The binding Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027 state the identity in one block: "Name of the course in English: Structural and Geotechnical Engineering | Class: LM-23 - Civil Engineering | Course language: Italian and English | Course delivery methods: conventional study course", and the same regulations say in terms: "the course of study is not divided into specific curricula" (Italian original: "il corso di studi non è articolato in specifici curricula"). WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS is a fully tabulated ENGLISH-LANGUAGE PATHWAY (Italian: "percorso formativo interamente in lingua inglese"), marketed in English as the "MSc in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering" and labelled "Curriculum in English" in the site menu. The orientation portal describes the arrangement precisely: "La Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica (STReGA)... è un corso di studi bilingue, offrendo anche un percorso formativo interamente in lingua inglese (MSc in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering)" — in the portal's own English rendering, "is a bilingual program that also offers a track taught entirely in English". So the brief's note that the programme is self-described as a "corso di studi bilingue" is CONFIRMED verbatim; only the word "curriculum" is wrong in the University's technical vocabulary. PRACTICAL EFFECT FOR AN APPLICANT: you do not apply to a separate programme, and the diploma does not name a track. ITALIAN DIPLOMA TITLE: "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica" (class LM-23). English degree title used officially: "Master's Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering". The English pathway is a set of English-taught courses tabulated inside the single study plan; for each mandatory subject the student chooses either the Italian course or its English twin. The 2026/2027 Study Plan (Annex 1.2) heads the English block "Course in English — Possibility for the student to opt for the route entirely in English". ADMINISTERING DEPARTMENT: Dipartimento di Strutture per l'Ingegneria e l'Architettura (DiSt / DIST — Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture), department code 040129. SCHOOL: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School, SPSB). Teaching area (area didattica) recorded centrally: "Ingegneria". Duration 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS. level: master — Italian "Laurea Magistrale" (second-cycle degree), 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS. This CONFIRMS the research brief's "level: master". The central unina.it course record states "Tipo di corso: Magistrale", "Durata: 2 anni", "Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 1° livello". The orientation portal fact-sheet is headed "Master's Degree — Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica (STReGA)" with "Degree required Laurea I Livello". Art. 9 of the Didactic Regulations: "The legal duration of the Degree Program is two years." CREDIT AND EXAM STRUCTURE: "The master's degree is obtained by acquiring 120 ECTS by passing the exams, in a number NOT EXCEEDING 12, and the performance of other training activities" — the 12-exam ceiling is a hard ministerial cap (D.M. 16.3.2007) and it shapes the whole design of the programme, which is built almost entirely out of 9-CFU modules. Credits fall under five Types of Training Activity (TAF): B) characterising, C) related or supplementary, D) activity of the student's choice, E) final examination, F) further training activities. Each CFU = 25 hours of total student workload; a frontal lecture CFU = 8 contact hours (so a 9-CFU course = 72 hours), an internship CFU = 25 hours. STRUCTURE OF THE ENGLISH PATHWAY, a.y. 2026/2027 (from Annex 1.2, the current Study Plan). YEAR 1: "Fundamentals of Structural and Geotechnical Engineering" — an integrated 9-ECTS course in three modules (Module 1 Geotechnical Engineering CEAR-05/A, Module 2 Continuum Mechanics CEAR-06/A, Module 3 Structural Engineering CEAR-07/A), mandatory; Earthquake Engineering and Structural Control (9, CEAR-07/A, sem. 1, mandatory); Limit Analysis of Structures (9, CEAR-06/A, sem. 1, mandatory); Structural Mechanics OR Structural Analysis and Design (9, sem. 1, OPTIONAL); Static and Seismic Foundation Design (9, CEAR-05/A, sem. 2, mandatory); Theory and Design of Reinforced Concrete Structures OR Assessment and Retrofit of Structures (9, CEAR-07/A, one of your choice); Theory and Design of Steel Constructions OR Advanced Metallic Structures (9, CEAR-07/A, one of your choice); Advanced Applied Engineering Mathematics (9, MATH-04/A, sem. 2, OPTIONAL). YEAR 2 — TWO of your choice from semester 1: FEM in Non-linear Structural Analysis (CEAR-06/A), Mechanics of Composite and Advanced Materials (CEAR-06/A), Assessment and Retrofit of r.c. Structures (CEAR-07/A), Theory and Design of Bridges (CEAR-07/A), Structural Reliability (CEAR-07/A); TWO of your choice from semester 2: Advanced Metallic Structures (CEAR-07/A), Advanced Applied Engineering Mathematics (MATH-04/A), Innovative Building Materials (CEAR-07/A), Geotechnical Modelling (CEAR-05/A), Tunnels and Underground Structures (CEAR-05/A) — all 9 ECTS each. Plus one 9-CFU "Activity of choice from Table B" (TAF D), an INTERNSHIP and a THESIS DISSERTATION of 12 CFU (TAF E). Three second-year semester-2 subjects (Innovative Building Materials, Geotechnical Modelling, Tunnels and Underground Structures) "can be brought forward to the first year, subject to verification of the Bachelor's degree course and individual study plan by the Study Plan Committee". [uncertain] THE INTERNSHIP CFU FIGURE IS INCONSISTENT INSIDE THE SAME 2026/2027 DOCUMENT: the base (Italian) curriculum table records "Internship — 8 CFU — 200 hours — TAF F — Mandatory" plus a separate 1-CFU TAF F line "Knowledge of the English language", while the English-pathway table records "Internship — 9 CFU — 225 hours — TAF F — Mandatory" and carries no separate 1-CFU English line. The orientation portal sides with the 8-CFU reading: "L'attività di tirocinio, complessivamente, prevede un impegno di 200 ore (8 CFU) per gli studenti immatricolati a partire dall'a.a. 2023/2024, mentre è previsto un impegno di 225 ore (9 CFU) per gli studenti immatricolati negli anni precedenti" — i.e. 9 CFU/225 h is the OLD pre-2023/24 rule, so the English-pathway table appears to carry a stale row. Either way the total is 120 CFU. FINAL EXAM (Art. 16): "The final examination consists of the discussion of a master's thesis prepared by the student in an original manner under the guidance of one or more supervisors, at least one of whom is a lecturer at the University of Naples Federico II." The thesis is a design project or a monographic, theoretical and/or experimental study, and "may also be written in English, especially where the work has been carried out within research projects or internationalisation programmes" — the orientation portal adds that in that case "ad esso deve essere allegato un estratto in lingua italiana" (an Italian-language abstract must be attached). The presentation lasts "as a rule 15 minutes", before a Commission chaired by the Degree Programme Coordinator. The final mark weighs the CFU-weighted exam average expressed in 110ths, the quality of the thesis and presentation, the duration of the master's, and meritorious activities such as Erasmus or the Double Degree. Graduates may sit the Italian State Examination and register in Section A of the Register of Engineers. ATTENDANCE (Art. 10) IS STRICTER THAN AT MOST FEDERICO II DEGREES: "as a rule, attendance is compulsory for all training activities"; for courses including Laboratory activity, attendance at at least 70% is a prerequisite for assessment; where in-itinere tests are used, having taken at least 70% of them is a prerequisite; and "attendance at seminar activities that award training credits is compulsory".
teaching_language: BILINGUAL BY DESIGN — Italian and English — with a complete, officially tabulated pathway that can be taken ENTIRELY IN ENGLISH. This is the single most important thing to understand about this degree, and it is a materially different arrangement from a standard English-taught programme. THE OFFICIAL LABELS. The orientation portal fact-sheet header records "Lingua ITA/ENG" (English version: "Language ENG/ITA") — a PAIRED value, not the single "ENG" used for wholly English-taught Federico II degrees. The 2026/2027 Didactic Regulations record "Course language: Italian and English". Art. 1 states: "The CdS in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering is hinged in Civil Engineering, Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture and is a course of study with an international character, AS IT ALSO ENVISAGES A COURSE OF STUDY ENTIRELY IN ENGLISH." Art. 2 elaborates: "The Master Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering is international in character, in that it also provides a course of study entirely in English (Master Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering), which represents a DIFFERENT PATHWAY FOR ACHIEVING THE SAME SPECIFIC EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES. This pathway is tabulated in the course regulations, so as to be clearly identifiable by the student, although it simply gathers together teachings that are SUBSTANTIALLY EQUIVALENT TO THOSE IN ITALIAN." HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE — THE PAIRING MECHANISM. The 2026/2027 Study Plan pairs each mandatory Italian course with its English twin and marks the pair "Mandatory (one of your choice)". Concrete examples from the base table: "Fondazioni - I semester" (CEAR-05/A) is paired with "Static and seismic foundation design - II semester" (CEAR-05/A); "Dinamica delle Costruzioni ed ingegneria Sismica - I semester" (CEAR-07/A) is paired with "Earthquake engineering and structural control - I semester" (CEAR-07/A); "Teoria e Progetto delle costruzioni in c.a." is paired with "Theory and design of reinforced concrete structures". So the student picks a language per subject. The Regulations describe the same design from the Italian side: the first three mandatory courses each "prevede l'alternativa fra un insegnamento in lingua italiana ed il corrispondente in lingua inglese", and of the sixteen Construction-Technique courses available for one free slot, "cinque dei quali in lingua inglese" (five of which are in English). THE ENGLISH PATHWAY IS COMPLETE AND SELF-SUFFICIENT for the taught component: the 2026/2027 Study Plan's dedicated English table (headed "Course in English — Possibility for the student to opt for the route entirely in English") supplies mandatory and elective courses covering the whole 120 CFU, and the programme's own site publishes it as "Curriculum in English". Every course in that table is delivered "Frontal lesson", "In presence" — there is no distance or blended component; Art. 7 records "The teaching activity is carried out in the conventional mode." WHY THE ENGLISH PATHWAY EXISTS, in the University's own words: "The English language pathway... aims to attract international students. This feature represents an important added value also for students of Italian nationality enrolled in this course, as they will be able to benefit from the advantages of their educational experience in a multi-cultural environment. The training offer in English is more oriented towards the training of an engineer destined to operate in a globalised market and ready to carry out his or her activity in international contexts." [uncertain] THE RESIDUAL ITALIAN-EXPOSURE RISK, AND IT IS REAL — THREE SLOTS. (1) THE 9-CFU TAF D FREE-CHOICE SLOT ("Activity of choice from Table B"): Art. 9 provides that "the student has freedom of choice among all the courses activated at the University, provided they are consistent with the training project", assessed by the CCD; the University-wide catalogue it draws on is overwhelmingly Italian-taught, so an English-only student must deliberately pick from the English rows of Table B. (2) THE 9-CFU TAF C SLOT "Course of your choice from Table B": same exposure, though Table B is drawn from Tables A1/A2/A3 which do contain the English courses. (3) THE SECOND-YEAR ELECTIVE POOL: the English table offers 5 courses in semester 1 and 5 in semester 2 from which 2 + 2 must be chosen, so the English pathway is workable but noticeably NARROWER than the Italian one (the Italian side offers sixteen Construction-Technique options for one slot, against five in English). An English-track student therefore has genuinely less elective freedom. (4) ADMINISTRATIVE AND STUDENT-LIFE ITALIAN: the Study Plan forms (Form A, Form A Minor, Form B) and much departmental correspondence are Italian-first, and foreign-citizenship students must enrol IN PERSON at the Segreteria counter rather than online. WHAT IS NOT REQUIRED: NO ITALIAN-LANGUAGE QUALIFICATION IS REQUIRED to be admitted or to graduate on the English pathway. There is no Italian examination anywhere in the study plan, and the 1-CFU TAF F language item is "Knowledge of the ENGLISH language", not Italian. Free optional Italian courses for international students are available through the University Language Centre (CLA, https://www.cla.unina.it/). THESIS LANGUAGE: may be written in English (with an Italian abstract attached); in the Double Degree it MUST be written in English.

degree_class: LM-23 — Italian degree class LM-23 "Ingegneria civile" (Civil Engineering). This CONFIRMS the degree_class given in the research brief, and it is stated identically across every official source, with no conflict anywhere: (a) the orientation portal fact-sheet header — "Classe di laurea LM-23" / "Degree class LM-23"; (b) the central unina.it course record — "Classe di Laurea: LM-23 Ingegneria civile"; (c) the DiSt department page — "LM-23 Ingegneria civile"; (d) the Didactic Regulations cover page — "REGOLAMENTO DIDATTICO DEL CORSO DI STUDI LAUREA MAGISTRALE IN INGEGNERIA STRUTTURALE E GEOTECNICA — CLASSE LM-23", and the 2026/2027 English version's Art. 1 identity block — "Class: LM-23 – Civil Engineering"; (e) the 2026/2027 Study Plan (Annex 1.2) header — "MASTER'S DEGREE IN STRUCTURAL AND GEOTECHNICAL ENGINEERING, CLASS LM-23". The double-degree agreement also awards the LM-23 title explicitly: the orientation portal describes it as "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica (classe LM-23 – classe delle Lauree Magistrali in Ingegneria Civile) rilasciato dall'Università degli studi di Napoli Federico II". ADMINISTRATIVE COORDINATES THAT GO WITH THE CLASS: Area didattica "Ingegneria"; Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base; Dipartimento di Strutture per l'Ingegneria e l'Architettura; Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Ingegneria. Unlike some Federico II engineering-class degrees administered by a science department, here the class, the school, the department and the student-records office are all consistently on the Engineering side. PROFESSIONAL CONSEQUENCE OF LM-23: graduates may sit the Italian State Examination (Esame di Stato) and register in SECTION A of the Register of Engineers (Albo degli Ingegneri) — the full professional-engineer register.
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS WITH A COMPULSORY ADMISSION CHECK — the orientation portal fact-sheet records the admission mode literally as "Accesso: VERIFICA DI PREPARAZIONE" (English version: "Admission: Verifica di preparazione", i.e. "preparation check"). There is NO numerus clausus, NO seat cap, NO ranked competitive selection and NO admission examination — but there is also no automatic right of entry, and this programme's gate is genuinely stricter and more quantified than the bare "open access" label used by many Federico II master's degrees. NOT A RESTRICTED-ACCESS COURSE: the programme does not appear in the University's index of "Corsi a numero programmato" and no bando di ammissione is published for it (see official_call_url). THE TWO COMPULSORY GATES (Art. 4 and Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027): "specific access criteria are envisaged concerning the possession of CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (in terms of specific CFUs obtained in sets of SSDs) and the COMPULSORY VERIFICATION OF THE ADEQUACY OF THE STUDENT'S PERSONAL PREPARATION." Art. 5 puts it beyond doubt: "Verification of personal preparation is ALWAYS MANDATORY, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it." The Italian original is blunter still: "La verifica della personale preparazione è obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari." The School-level framework is set by Decree of the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base, DP no. 18 of 12/02/2015. WHAT MAKES THIS PROGRAMME UNUSUAL IS THAT THE CHECK IS NUMERIC AND PUBLISHED, not discretionary: there is a published minimum-CFU-per-SSD table AND a published minimum grade-average table (see academic_requirements). Federico II degrees that publish an explicit GPA threshold are the minority. THE PROGRAMME'S OWN PRE-SCREENING ROUTE — THE MOST IMPORTANT PRACTICAL INSTRUCTION ON THE WHOLE SITE, and it applies squarely to international applicants: "Those who, wishing to enroll in the Master's Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering, show gaps in curricular requirements in SSD CFU AND/OR HAVE AN AVERAGE RATING LOWER THAN 24/30, BEFORE FORMALIZING THE ENROLLMENT MUST SEND A PRE-EVALUATION REQUEST TO THE TEACHING OFFICE FILLING IN THE FORM A available in Forms section. In this way, the Study Plan Commission will indicate to the student how to compile his/her study plan in order to recover possible educational gaps." Form A is at https://strega.unina.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Form-A.pdf and is sent digitally to didattica.dist@unina.it. Note the 24/30 trigger: since a foreign transcript will rarely map cleanly onto the Italian 30-point scale, most non-Italian applicants should assume the pre-evaluation route applies to them. THE THREE APPLICANT ROUTES. (1) ITALIAN-QUALIFICATION APPLICANTS enrol online at www.segrepass.unina.it and are checked by the Segreteria. (2) EU APPLICANTS AND APPLICANTS LEGALLY RESIDENT IN THE EU holding a foreign qualification have "unrestricted access to university courses if you hold a foreign qualification corresponding to the required Italian qualification. In this case you have to send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements" (international.unina.it). (3) NON-EU APPLICANTS RESIDING ABROAD must pre-enrol on the ministerial UNIVERSITALY portal, be evaluated, and obtain a pre-acceptance letter from the Programme Coordinator before a visa can be issued. The University warns: "pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes. In order to matriculate you also need to take and pass the verifications of the entry requirements and the admission procedures set for the degree programme of your interest", and "Important! The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa." A SEPARATE, GENUINELY COMPETITIVE SELECTION EXISTS FOR THE DOUBLE DEGREE (not for admission to the degree itself): only "a maximum of 5 (five) students is admitted" to the UNINA-IST Lisbon pathway, ranked on degree grade, academic average, extracurricular experience and motivation, with the youngest candidate preferred on a tie. Applicants must already be enrolled in year 1 at UNINA (or enrol by 31 December of year 1, admitted with reserve).
academic_requirements:
A first-cycle degree in CIVIL AND ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING (or a foreign equivalent), PLUS a published minimum-CFU-per-SSD profile, PLUS a published minimum grade average, PLUS English at B2. Unusually for Federico II, all four are quantified in the binding regulations rather than left to discretion.

(A) DEGREE-CLASS ROUTE (Art. 4.1, Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027, verbatim): "To be admitted to the Master's Degree Course in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering (STReGA in the following), one must hold a university degree or another qualification obtained abroad that is recognised as suitable. The curricular requirements for admission are - as a rule - automatically possessed by graduates of the degree courses of class no. 8 in civil and environmental engineering pursuant to Ministerial Decree 509/99 and the degree courses of class L-7 in civil and environmental engineering pursuant to Ministerial Decree 270/04 WHO HAVE FOLLOWED THE GENERALIST OR PASSING CURRICULUM." Note how NARROW this is compared with most Federico II master's degrees: a single Italian bachelor class (L-7 / old class 8), and even then only the generalist or "passante" track is automatically sufficient. There is no long list of admissible classes.

(B) THE MINIMUM-CFU TABLE — the hard quantified requirement, and the thing an international applicant must actually check line by line against their transcript. "Enrolment on the course is not permitted if MORE THAN 27 CFUs of the minimum curricular requirements specified in the following table are lacking." The 2026/2027 table (in post-2023 SSD codes) reads: MATH/02 + MAT/03 — 18 CFU minimum; PHYS-01/03 — 6; CEAR-01/A + CEAR-01/B — 9 (*); CEAR-03/A + CEAR-03/B — 9; CEAR-05 — 9 (**); MATH-04 + CEAR-06 — 18; CEAR-07 — 15; CEAR-04 + CEAR-08 + CEAR-10 — 9. TOTAL 93 CFU. Footnotes: "(*) Students who have already completed 6 CFU in SSD CEAR-01/A and CEAR-01/B can make up for it with a 3 CFU Supplementary Colloquium in SSD CEAR-01/A. (**) Students who have already completed 6 CFU in SSD CEAR-05 can make up for it with a 3 CFU Supplementary Colloquium in SSD CEAR-05." The PREVIOUS (a.y. 2024/2025) Italian regulations expressed exactly the same profile in the OLD SSD codes, which are far easier to read and are given here as the plain-language key: MAT/03 + MAT/05 (analysis/numerical analysis) 18; FIS/01 (physics) 6; ICAR/01 + ICAR/02 (hydraulics, maritime/hydrology) 9; ICAR/04 + ICAR/05 (roads/railways, transport) 9; ICAR/07 (GEOTECHNICS) 9; MAT/07 + ICAR/08 (mathematical physics, STRUCTURAL MECHANICS/SCIENZA DELLE COSTRUZIONI) 18; ICAR/09 (TECNICA DELLE COSTRUZIONI — structural design) 15; ICAR/06 + ICAR/10 + ICAR/17 (surveying, building technology, drawing) 9. IN PLAIN TERMS: expect to need roughly 18 CFU of mathematics, 6 of physics, 9 of hydraulics, 9 of transport infrastructure, 9 of geotechnics, 18 of structural mechanics, 15 of structural design and 9 of surveying/building technology. A generic mechanical, architectural or non-civil engineering bachelor will typically FAIL this table, chiefly on ICAR/09, ICAR/07 and ICAR/01-02.

(C) WHAT HAPPENS IF YOU ARE SHORT — a three-tier rule, and it is more forgiving than it first looks: (i) SHORTFALL UP TO 27 CFU: "Graduates who do not meet these requirements for an overall difference not exceeding 27 CFU will be allowed to propose, AS PART OF the 120 CFU envisaged for the Master's degree, an educational pathway that envisages the passing of examinations of the degree course such as to compensate for the existing deficiencies" — i.e. you are admitted and make up the gap inside the normal 120 CFU (this is what the "Additional training requirements, if necessary (Table C)" row worth "0/9/18" CFU in year 1 of the English pathway is for). (ii) SHORTFALL BEYOND 27 CFU BUT ≤ 18 CFU OF EXTRA INTEGRATIONS: agreed with the Study Plan Committee and added ON TOP, "included in the study plan that will provide MORE THAN 120 CFU for the Master's Degree". (iii) LARGER SHORTFALL: "the corresponding credits must necessarily be acquired PRIOR TO ENROLMENT in the Master's Degree Course", via single course units (corsi singoli) or by enrolling in Federico II's Civil Engineering bachelor with an abbreviated course. Credits earned as single courses may later be recognised up to a ceiling of 36 CFU.

(D) THE GRADE-AVERAGE GATE (Art. 4.2, "Verification of student's personal preparation") — applies to everyone enrolled after 1 September 2011 and is computed from "the average M of the marks (in thirtieths) obtained in the proficiency examinations for the degree, weighted on the basis of the relative consistencies in CFUs, as well as the duration of studies D1 expressed in course years, compared with the normal duration D2 of the course". AUTOMATIC ADMISSION CRITERIA: if you finished on time (D1=D2) you need M ≥ 21/30; one year over (D1=D2+1) M ≥ 22.5/30; two or more years over (D1 ≥ D2+2) M ≥ 24/30. The 2024/2025 Italian version of the same table carried an ADDITIONAL COLUMN that the 2026/2027 English version omits: "Studenti provenienti da altri Atenei — D1 qualunque — M ≥ 24", i.e. applicants from ANOTHER UNIVERSITY needed M ≥ 24/30 regardless of duration. Since virtually every international applicant comes from another university, this is the threshold to plan against — and it is exactly the 24/30 figure that the Study Plan page uses as its Form A pre-evaluation trigger. FALLING SHORT IS NOT FATAL: "In the presence of applications for admission... from students who do not meet the criteria for automatic admission, the relevant Academic Coordination Committee examines the applications on the basis of the curriculum acquired and, in the event of a positive assessment, prepares supplementary assessment procedures to verify the personal preparation of these students. The assessment may provide for the identification of a training debt and the consequent allocation of an Additional Training Obligation (OFA)."

(E) THE FOREIGN-APPLICANT WORDING — softer, and the most quotable line for a non-Italian reader. The programme's own FAQ, under "What are the entry requirements for the English-taught programme?", answers: "BACHELOR IN CIVIL ENGINEERING OR AN EQUIVALENT DEGREE. Equivalence shall be evaluated by a dedicated internal committee upon scrutiny of your TRANSCRIPT OF RECORDS (reporting a detailed summary of the exams passed for the BSc)." So for an international applicant the operative test is a transcript-based equivalence judgement by an internal committee, not mechanical class-matching — but the committee will be reading the transcript against the CFU/SSD table in (B).

[uncertain] FOUR UNRESOLVED POINTS: (1) the 2026/2027 SSD table contains an evident transcription error — the physics row is printed as "PHYS-01/03???", question marks and all, where the 2024/2025 table cleanly read "FIS/01 — 6"; (2) the 2026/2027 table drops the "students from other universities: M ≥ 24" column without explanation, so it is unclear whether that stricter threshold still formally binds international applicants (assume it does); (3) the mixture of code generations in the same table ("MATH/02, MAT/03" combines a new-style and an old-style code) suggests the table was only partially updated; (4) no minimum overall degree classification, no GRE/GMAT and no prerequisite reading list are published. Confirm your own case with didattica.dist@unina.it BEFORE applying — the programme explicitly invites this through Form A.
entry_exam_or_test:
NO ADMISSION EXAMINATION OF ANY KIND — no written test, no TOLC, no TOLC-I, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT, no portfolio, and no compulsory interview. What replaces a test is a DOCUMENTARY assessment carried out by the Didactic Coordination Commission (CCD) and the Study Plan Committee, plus — only in specific circumstances — a small supplementary oral colloquium.

NO TOLC: the TOLC is used by the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base for BACHELOR-level admission only. For two-year master's degrees the School applies the DM 270/04 framework instead: verification of curricular requirements plus verification of personal preparation, governed by the School's Decree DP no. 18 of 12/02/2015. Neither the Didactic Regulations, the orientation portal, the programme site nor the FAQ mentions any entrance test for STReGA.

THE ACTUAL ASSESSMENT — three components, all documentary: (1) CURRICULAR CHECK against the published minimum-CFU-per-SSD table (see academic_requirements); (2) PERSONAL-PREPARATION CHECK against the published grade-average thresholds (M ≥ 21 / 22.5 / 24 in thirtieths, depending on how long the bachelor took; M ≥ 24 for applicants from other universities under the 2024/25 wording). Art. 5: "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it."; (3) for international applicants specifically, an EQUIVALENCE JUDGEMENT ON THE TRANSCRIPT: the FAQ states "Equivalence shall be evaluated by A DEDICATED INTERNAL COMMITTEE UPON SCRUTINY OF YOUR TRANSCRIPT OF RECORDS (reporting a detailed summary of the exams passed for the BSc)."

THE ONE ORAL ELEMENT THAT DOES EXIST — AND IT IS NOT AN ENTRANCE INTERVIEW. The regulations provide two narrowly-scoped 3-CFU "Supplementary Colloquia" (colloquio integrativo) used purely to close a small credit gap: "(*) Students who have already completed 6 CFU in SSD CEAR-01/A and CEAR-01/B can make up for it with a 3 CFU Supplementary Colloquium in SSD CEAR-01/A. (**) Students who have already completed 6 CFU in SSD CEAR-05 can make up for it with a 3 CFU Supplementary Colloquium in SSD CEAR-05." These are credit-recovery colloquia in hydraulics/maritime and geotechnics respectively, taken by students who are 3 CFU short — not a competitive interview and not a filter for everyone.

IF YOU MISS THE AUTOMATIC CRITERIA: no examination follows automatically; instead "the relevant Academic Coordination Committee examines the applications on the basis of the curriculum acquired and, in the event of a positive assessment, PREPARES SUPPLEMENTARY ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES to verify the personal preparation of these students. The assessment may provide for the identification of a training debt and the consequent allocation of an Additional Training Obligation (OFA), the procedures for the extinction of which are regulated (DP 18 of 12 February 2015)." So a bespoke assessment CAN be imposed on a case-by-case basis, but its content, format and language are not published.

THE PROCEDURAL STEP THAT REPLACES AN ENTRANCE EXAM, AND WHICH MOST INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS WILL TRIGGER: "Those who... show gaps in curricular requirements in SSD CFU and/or have an average rating lower than 24/30, BEFORE FORMALIZING THE ENROLLMENT must send a pre-evaluation request to the Teaching Office filling in the FORM A". Form A is titled "Verification of curricular and personal preparation requirements for access and presentation of the study plan" and is emailed to didattica.dist@unina.it. Treat submitting Form A early as the real first step of applying to this programme.

THE ENGLISH GATE IS A TEST, BUT A LANGUAGE ONE, AND IT SITS AFTER ENROLMENT: a student without an accepted B2 certificate "may take a test at the CLA (University Language Center) to assess B2-level proficiency. If the test result is negative, the student may take a 'tailored' course with a final exam, also organized by the CLA, to verify attainment of the B2 level." See language_requirements.

[uncertain] For NON-EU applicants going through Universitaly, no unina.it page for THIS programme states whether the pre-acceptance evaluation includes an interview. Several other Federico II English-taught degrees do warn of a probable interview; STReGA does not mention one either way. Assume a documentary evaluation, but be prepared for the Programme Committee to request a short online conversation about your background.
seats_total: NO SEAT CAP — no total number of places is set or published for this programme. The orientation portal records the admission mode as "Accesso: Verifica di preparazione" (a preparation check), NOT "numero programmato"; the programme does not appear in the University's index of restricted-access courses ("Corsi a numero programmato") for a.y. 2026/2027; no bando di ammissione exists for it; and neither the Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027, the 2026/2027 Study Plan, the DiSt department page nor the central unina.it course record states a number of places or an "utenza sostenibile" figure. Art. 5.1 of the Regulations leaves scheduling to the CCD in general terms — "The CCD of the Degree Program normally regulates the admission criteria and any scheduling of enrolments, except in cases subject to different provisions of law" — without fixing any quota. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR AN APPLICANT: there is no cut-off score to beat and no ranking list to climb. Your admission depends entirely on your own transcript meeting the published CFU/SSD table and grade-average thresholds, not on competition with other candidates. This is a genuinely different risk profile from a capped programme — you can assess your own chances in advance from the published tables. THE NUMBERS THAT DO EXIST ARE FOR SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY, and should not be mistaken for admission quotas: (a) the DOUBLE DEGREE with Instituto Superior Técnico Lisbon is capped — "A maximum of 5 (five) students is admitted to attend the course" — but that is a selection for a mobility pathway, open only to students ALREADY enrolled in year 1 at UNINA; (b) the Department's scholarship scheme for international students offered "n. 3 (tre) borse di studio" for a.y. 2025/2026 — again a funding competition, not an admission quota, and losing it does not affect admission; (c) the University-wide tutoring scheme makes "120 Tutors" available across the whole Polytechnic School. [uncertain] MARKED UNCERTAIN ONLY BECAUSE A NULL IS BEING REPORTED RATHER THAN A PUBLISHED NUMBER: no unina.it page states a figure, and none says in so many words that intake is unlimited. The absence of a cap is inferred from the "Verifica di preparazione" classification, the absence of a bando and the absence of the programme from the numero-programmato index — which is strong but indirect evidence.
non_eu_reserved_seats: NONE PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT — because the programme has no seat cap at all (see seats_total), no reserved sub-quota for non-EU applicants residing abroad appears on any University of Naples Federico II page for this degree. Neither the Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027, the 2026/2027 Study Plan, the programme site strega.unina.it, the DiSt department page, the orientation portal fact sheet nor international.unina.it states a non-EU contingent for Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica. [uncertain] WITH ONE STRUCTURAL CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY ITALIAN DEGREE: Italian universities must still declare an annual contingent of places for non-EU visa students on the ministerial UNIVERSITALY portal even for open-access courses, and that per-course figure is published on universitaly.it — a domain outside the unina.it-only source restriction imposed by this research task. It could therefore not be verified here. Applicants should check the STReGA entry on universitaly.it for their target intake year, and write to didattica.dist@unina.it in parallel. WHAT UNINA.IT DOES PUBLISH IS A CAPACITY CONSTRAINT EXPRESSED AS A DATE RATHER THAN A NUMBER, and for an open-access programme this is the binding practical limit: "JUNE – 15 – 2026 – Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. AFTER THIS DATE PRE-ENROLMENT IS ALLOWED TO THE PROGRAMMES WITH RESTRICTED ACCESS ONLY." Because STReGA is NOT a restricted-access programme, non-EU pre-enrolment for it simply CLOSES on that date and does not reopen — the practical effect of a quota, delivered as a cut-off date. A REAL, SEPARATE NUMBER THAT NON-EU APPLICANTS SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture runs a scholarship scheme reserved to international students — "The selection process concerns the awarding of 3 (three) scholarships, each with a duration of 2 years and a total amount of € 12,000.00" (a.y. 2025/2026 call). Eligibility is automatic for "All foreign students regularly registered on Universitaly by the deadline of MAY 31 and who have been previously admitted to the first year", and "The submission of an application for participation is not required." That is three FUNDED places, not three admission places — everyone else who qualifies academically is still admitted. NON-EU APPLICANTS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU are treated like EU applicants: they do not pre-enrol on Universitaly, are not subject to any contingent, and follow the calendar in application_deadline_eu instead.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH AT CEFR B2 — a formal requirement written into the Didactic Regulations, applying to ALL students of this degree (not only those on the English pathway), and enforceable after enrolment through the University Language Centre. ITALIAN IS NOT REQUIRED at admission, for the visa, or for graduation on the English pathway.

THE REQUIREMENT (Art. 4.3 "Knowledge of English", Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027, verbatim): "Graduates of the Master's program in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering must be able to use at least one European Union language other than Italian—specifically English—fluently in both written and oral communication, WITH PROFICIENCY EQUIVALENT TO LEVEL B2. To this end, the program includes 1 credit hour of additional language training." Art. 4 adds that the access requirements include "the documented ability to use English fluently, in written and oral form, WITH REFERENCE ALSO TO DISCIPLINARY TERMINOLOGY" (Italian original: "la documentata capacità di utilizzare fluentemente, in forma scritta e orale, la lingua inglese con riferimento anche ai lessici disciplinari") — note that the standard is explicitly technical English, not general English.

WHICH CERTIFICATES ARE ACCEPTED — and this programme is NOTABLY MORE FLEXIBLE than most Federico II degrees. The programme's FAQ, answering "What are the entry requirements for the English-taught programme?", states: "Knowledge of the English language with a CERTIFICATION OF LEVEL B2 AS A MINIMUM. The most common certifications (TOEFL, IELTS, CAMBRIDGE, TRINITY COLLEGE LONDON, PEARSON) are certainly acceptable. A DEDICATED COMMITTEE SHALL EVALUATE THE SUITABILITY OF MORE INFORMAL CERTIFICATIONS, LIKE THOSE ISSUED BY UNIVERSITIES WHOSE OFFICIAL TEACHING LANGUAGE IS ENGLISH." TWO POINTS WORTH STRESSING: (i) the named list — TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, Trinity College London, Pearson — is illustrative ("the most common"), not closed; (ii) AN ENGLISH-MEDIUM BACHELOR'S DEGREE CAN BE OFFERED IN PLACE OF A TEST and will be considered on its merits by a committee. Many comparable Federico II programmes refuse this outright, and several impose a two-year recency rule on the certificate; NO RECENCY LIMIT IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE FOR STReGA.

ENFORCEMENT — RECOMMENDED AT ENTRY, MANDATORY BY GRADUATION, WITH A UNIVERSITY-RUN FALLBACK: "It is RECOMMENDED that students meet this requirement at the start of the program: upon enrollment, students may submit appropriate certification of B2-level English proficiency, which will be reviewed and, if applicable, recognized by the Program Committee. IN THE ABSENCE OF SUCH CERTIFICATION, THE STUDENT MAY TAKE A TEST AT THE CLA (University Language Center) to assess B2-level proficiency. If the test result is negative, the student may take a 'TAILORED' COURSE WITH A FINAL EXAM, also organized by the CLA, to verify attainment of the B2 level of English proficiency." The B2 requirement is carried in the study plan as a 1-CFU TAF F item literally named "Knowledge of the English language", so it is a graduation requirement discharged through the CLA (https://www.cla.unina.it/), not merely an entry filter. The word "recommended" is important: unlike some Federico II degrees, a missing certificate does not by itself block enrolment — it just has to be cleared before you graduate.

ITALIAN — NOT REQUIRED. There is no Italian-language examination anywhere in the study plan, and the 1-CFU language item is for ENGLISH. The University-wide rule for English-taught courses applies: "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required. Remember that an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation." Free optional Italian courses are offered to international students by the CLA. [uncertain] TWO DRAFTING GAPS TO BE AWARE OF. (1) THE ITALIAN-EXEMPTION SENTENCE ON international.unina.it OMITS TWO-YEAR MASTER'S DEGREES: it enumerates "three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH", whereas the parallel clause imposing B2 Italian for Italian-taught courses does expressly name "magistral degree course". By symmetry, and given that STReGA attaches no Italian condition to any credit, an English-pathway student is plainly intended to be exempt — but the University's own sentence does not name two-year master's degrees in the exemption. (2) BECAUSE STReGA IS FORMALLY A BILINGUAL (ITA/ENG) DEGREE RATHER THAN A WHOLLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT ONE, a consular officer or a Universitaly reviewer could in principle read the course as "taught in Italian" and ask for B2 Italian. Nothing on unina.it says this happens, but applicants relying on the exemption should upload their English certificate to Universitaly, keep the Art. 4.3 text and the FAQ answer to hand, and confirm with didattica.dist@unina.it and gdellaco@unina.it (Internationalisation referent) before their visa appointment. LANGUAGE OF THE THESIS: may be written in English, "especially where the work has been carried out within research projects or internationalisation programmes", with an Italian-language abstract attached; in the Double Degree the thesis MUST be in English. SCHOLARSHIP BONUS: in the Department's international scholarship ranking, "official English and (IF AVAILABLE) ITALIAN language certifications" are worth up to 7 of the 30 points — so an Italian certificate, while never required, is worth real money here.
application_deadline_eu:
THERE IS NO COMPETITIVE APPLICATION DEADLINE for EU (and EU-equivalent) candidates, because the programme is open access with a preparation check: EU applicants do not compete for places, they enrol within the University's calendar once their qualification has been verified. FOUR SETS OF DATES APPLY, and they do not all agree — read to the end.

(A) QUALIFICATION EVALUATION — NO FIXED DATE, DO IT FIRST AND EARLY. Per international.unina.it, an EU candidate (or any candidate legally resident in the EU) holding a FOREIGN qualification must "send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements". For this programme, send to didattica.dist@unina.it (Teaching Office) and/or glignola@unina.it (Coordinator).

(B) THE PROGRAMME'S OWN FORM A PRE-EVALUATION — the step most international applicants will need, and it has no published opening date, so start as soon as your transcript is final: "Those who... show gaps in curricular requirements in SSD CFU and/or have an average rating lower than 24/30, BEFORE FORMALIZING THE ENROLLMENT must send a pre-evaluation request to the Teaching Office filling in the form A."

(C) THE PROGRAMME/DEPARTMENT WINDOW — 1 SEPTEMBER to 31 OCTOBER. The orientation portal's "Termini e scadenze" section for this course states: "L'immatricolazione e l'iscrizione agli anni successivi hanno luogo, DI NORMA, DAL 1 SETTEMBRE AL 31 OTTOBRE DI OGNI ANNO". The same window governs the STUDY PLAN, which is a genuine STReGA-specific obligation with its own deadline: "1st September - 31st October for presentation of the study plan for the first enrolling in the LM STReGA; 1st September - 31st October for variation in a previously submitted study plan", and — the tighter rule — "THE STUDY PLAN MUST BE SUBMITTED WITHIN 15 DAYS FROM ENROLLMENT." Form B (changes to a plan already submitted) must be "delivered by OCTOBER 31st". The Commission then has 30 days to approve and transmit the plan to the Segreteria for upload to SegrePass. Individual study plans under Art. 11 c. 4-bis DM 270/2004 must be sent to didattica.dist@unina.it "entro 30 giorni dall'immatricolazione".

(D) THE BINDING UNIVERSITY ENROLMENT CALENDAR FOR A.Y. 2026/2027 ("Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27"), which governs Italian and EU students alike and is the document that actually controls payment and registration: 2026-07-16 — "Inizio periodo ordinario immatricolazione" (ordinary matriculation period opens); 2026-09-01 — start of the ordinary period for transfers between courses/universities; 2026-11-02 — "Scadenza periodo ordinario immatricolazione e iscrizione agli anni successivi" (ORDINARY DEADLINE) and deadline for the direct ISEEU data retrieval from INPS; 2026-11-03 — extraordinary (late) period opens; 2027-01-15 — last date to enrol late with a EUR 50 surcharge; 2027-01-16 — from this date the late surcharge rises to EUR 110; 2027-03-31 — ABSOLUTE FINAL DEADLINE for first-year enrolment in a two-year master's: "Le iscrizioni al primo anno dei corsi di laurea magistrali potranno essere effettuate entro il 31 marzo 2027", with the proviso that a Teaching Coordination Commission may require anyone enrolling after 2026-12-31 to first earn between 6 and 12 CFU through single course units (those single-course fees are refunded if the master's enrolment is completed by 31 March 2027). INSTALMENTS: 1st (60% + regional tax + stamp) by 2026-11-02; 2nd (20%) by 2027-03-01; 3rd (20%) by 2027-04-30; a EUR 100 surcharge applies from 2027-07-16 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments.

[uncertain] A DIRECT CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL UNINA SOURCES ON THE OPENING DATE, AND IT IS WIDER THAN THE USUAL WEEKEND ROLL-OVER. The orientation portal page for THIS COURSE says enrolment runs "di norma, dal 1 SETTEMBRE al 31 OTTOBRE", while the binding University guide opens the ordinary period on 16 JULY 2026 and closes it on 2 NOVEMBER 2026. The closing dates (31 October vs 2 November 2026) are reconcilable — 31 October 2026 is a Saturday and 2 November the following Monday — but the OPENING dates differ by six weeks. The most likely reading is that the University portal opens on 16 July while this Department's own counters, study-plan process and 1 September transfer window define the practical start for this course; note also that the portal hedges with "di norma". SAFE PLAN: be ready to act from 16 July 2026, have everything filed by 31 OCTOBER 2026, and treat 2 November 2026 as the outer administrative limit. Do not rely on the March 2027 fallback — it costs a full semester of teaching and can trigger the 6-12 CFU single-course precondition. Note also that the orientation portal still links the PREVIOUS year's enrolment guide (guida_studente_rapida_25_26.pdf), so the portal's own date text may be stale. AN IMPORTANT PROCEDURAL TRAP FOR FOREIGN CITIZENS, EU INCLUDED: online enrolment is NOT available to you. "Coloro che presentano una cittadinanza straniera dovranno effettuare l'iscrizione presso gli sportelli delle Segreterie Studenti, NON POTRANNO USARE LA PROCEDURA ON-LINE. Per questi studenti gli importi da pagare sono distinti solo in base alla cittadinanza (studenti comunitari oppure studenti extracomunitari)." Italian-qualification holders enrol online at www.segrepass.unina.it; everyone with foreign citizenship must attend the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Ingegneria counter in person, which requires being in Naples within the window. TEACHING CALENDAR CONTEXT: courses "can start as early as September/October and, generally, are held through the end of May/middle of June", with two semesters running September-February and February-July.
application_deadline_non_eu:
For NON-EU applicants RESIDING ABROAD there is a hard, ministry-driven pipeline for a.y. 2026/2027, and for THIS programme the first date is effectively final because the course is open-access:
— 2026-06-15: PRE-ENROLMENT APPLICATION DEADLINE on the UNIVERSITALY portal (www.universitaly.it), naming the University of Naples Federico II and this degree. Verbatim from international.unina.it: "JUNE – 15 – 2026 – Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. AFTER THIS DATE PRE-ENROLMENT IS ALLOWED TO THE PROGRAMMES WITH RESTRICTED ACCESS ONLY." THIS IS THE OPERATIVE DEADLINE: because Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica is open access ("Verifica di preparazione"), not restricted access, non-EU pre-enrolment for it CLOSES on 15 June 2026 and does NOT reopen.
— 2026-11-30: deadline for lodging the study-visa application at the Italian Embassy/Consulate — "NOVEMBER – 30 – 2026 – Deadline for submitting the Visa Application at Italian Embassies/Consulates."
— 2027-01-31: deadline for completing enrolment (matriculation) in Naples, per the University's official 2026/2027 booklet "Information for non-EU students with residency abroad"; after that date students not officially enrolled have their visa revoked and the Italian police authorities are notified.

[uncertain] AIM FOR 31 MAY, NOT 15 JUNE — THERE IS A REAL PROGRAMME-LEVEL DATE TWO WEEKS EARLIER. The Department's own scholarship call for international students fixes eligibility by reference to an earlier Universitaly cut-off: "All foreign students regularly registered on Universitaly BY THE DEADLINE OF MAY 31 and who have been previously admitted to the first year of the Master's degree course in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering... are eligible for the scholarship." Two consequences: (i) missing 31 May does not by itself cost you admission (the University-wide 15 June date still governs), but it DOES cost you any chance of the Department's EUR 12,000 scholarship, for which no separate application is possible; (ii) the phrase "PREVIOUSLY ADMITTED" confirms that the programme expects the academic evaluation to be COMPLETE before the Universitaly deadline — so the Form A / transcript evaluation with didattica.dist@unina.it should be started months earlier, realistically in late winter or early spring.

THE SEQUENCE, AND A CONTRADICTION IN THE UNIVERSITY'S ADVICE. international.unina.it advises "It is advisable to obtain the admission to your chosen programme BEFORE applying on Universitaly", and states that "A pre-acceptance letter certifies your eligibility for the selected degree programme. It is issued by the Programme Coordinator following an evaluation of the documents you have submitted" and that "The University will validate your application once the course coordinator has issued your pre-acceptance letter." The University also warns, in terms: "Be aware that PRE-ENROLMENT ALONE DOES NOT GRANT ADMISSION to degree programmes. In order to matriculate you also need to take and pass the verifications of the entry requirements and the admission procedures set for the degree programme of your interest", and "IMPORTANT! THE UNIVERSITY OF NAPLES FEDERICO II DOES NOT ISSUE ADMISSION LETTERS FOR OBTAINING A VISA" — only the pre-acceptance letter routed through Universitaly. Further warnings: "Pre-admission to the University does not guarantee the issuance of a visa, which is the sole responsibility of the Embassy or Consulate" and "The issuance of a visa does not automatically guarantee enrolment at the University."

AFTER ARRIVAL — a programme-specific, time-critical obligation that is easy to miss. The STReGA "Mind List" for international students instructs: "WITHIN 8 WORKING DAYS FROM YOUR ARRIVAL IN ITALY, you must go to the 'QUESTURA' in order to complete the paperwork. We suggest you to send an email to the International Welcome Desk (I.W.D.), they can help you with this and with some other procedures" (internationalwelcomedesk@unina.it). Final enrolment is completed IN PERSON at the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Ingegneria, and the Department's Educational Office at Via Claudio 21, Building 6, 1st floor is open Monday-Friday 09:30-13:00.

NON-EU APPLICANTS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU are treated like EU applicants: unrestricted access, no Universitaly pre-enrolment, and the calendar in application_deadline_eu applies instead.

[uncertain] TIMING NOTE FOR READERS, AND IT MATTERS: this record was compiled on 2026-08-30, by which date the 15 June 2026 non-EU pre-enrolment deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 HAD ALREADY PASSED. A non-EU applicant reading this must target A.Y. 2027/2028 and re-check every date when the new booklet is published (typically around May). Note also that the 31 January 2027 matriculation date comes from the University's non-EU booklet PDF, whose text could not be machine-extracted during this research (the file uses a non-standard font encoding); it is reported here from the University's published deadline schedule for the same academic year and is consistent with the 30 November 2026 visa date, but should be re-verified against the booklet directly.
required_documents:
[uncertain] THERE IS NO SINGLE CONSOLIDATED APPLICATION CHECKLIST FOR THIS PROGRAMME. The list below is assembled from the programme's own Form A process, its "Mind List" for international students, its FAQ, its scholarship call, and University-level sources — so the Teaching Office or the Study Plan Committee could request an additional item.

(1) PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ITEMS — the ones that distinguish STReGA from a generic Federico II application:
— FORM A, "Verification of curricular and personal preparation requirements for access and presentation of the study plan" (https://strega.unina.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Form-A.pdf), sent in digital format to didattica.dist@unina.it. Required BEFORE formalising enrolment by anyone with SSD credit gaps and/or an average below 24/30 — which in practice means most international applicants. "All the study plan forms must be sent in digital format to the email: didattica.dist@unina.it."
— A DETAILED TRANSCRIPT OF RECORDS. The FAQ is explicit that this is the document the decision turns on: "Equivalence shall be evaluated by a dedicated internal committee upon scrutiny of your Transcript of Records (REPORTING A DETAILED SUMMARY OF THE EXAMS PASSED FOR THE BSc)." It must be detailed enough to map your credits onto the Art. 4 SSD table (mathematics, physics, hydraulics, transport, geotechnics, structural mechanics, structural design, surveying/building technology) — so include credit values, contact hours and syllabi/course descriptions, not just titles and grades.
— A B2 ENGLISH CERTIFICATE (TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, Trinity College London, Pearson, or — subject to committee assessment — evidence that your degree was taught in English). No recency limit is published.
— FORM B if you later change an approved study plan (deliverable by 31 October); Form A Minor for the Minor TT pathway; Form AC for internship credit declarations.
— FOR THE DEPARTMENT SCHOLARSHIP (no separate application form; assessed automatically): a CV "including any certificates, LETTERS OF RECOMMENDATION, PORTFOLIO and other additional documents which are deemed useful by the candidate" — worth up to 23 of 30 points — plus "official English and (if available) Italian language certifications" worth up to 7 points. Uploading a strong CV, references and a portfolio to Universitaly therefore has direct financial value here even though none of it is formally required for admission.

(2) FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT ON UNIVERSITALY (uploaded as PDF), Master's track: Transcript of Records; final degree certificate; detailed course descriptions; additional documents such as language certificates, motivation letter and reference letters; the PRE-ACCEPTANCE LETTER from the Programme Coordinator; and either a Declaration of Value or the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND Statement of Verification jointly. The application itself needs personal data exactly as on the passport and the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested.

(3) QUALIFICATION-RECOGNITION DOCUMENTS (mandatory at enrolment): a DECLARATION OF VALUE (DoV) issued by an Italian Embassy/Consulate in the country where the degree was obtained, OR a certificate of validity issued by ENIC-NARIC / CIMEA (https://www.cimea.it/EN/). For EU/EU-resident applicants the University asks for "any documentation that the University deems necessary for the evaluation of the foreign qualification: eventual translations; legalisations; DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT; certificates of examinations; certificates from the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA); any declarations of value issued by the competent diplomatic representations."

(4) FOR THE ITALIAN EMBASSY / VISA: the Universitaly pre-enrolment summary validated by the University; language certificates; health insurance; suitable accommodation; and proof of means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year ("proven by means of personal financial guarantees or those of parents or Italian or foreign citizens legally residing in Italian territory, or provided by Italian institutions and bodies of proven credit"). NOTE: the same page also carries EUR 6,079.45/year (EUR 467.95/month), but that figure relates to RESIDENCE-PERMIT RENEWAL, not the entry visa.

(5) ON ARRIVAL — the programme's own "MIND LIST — What you need to bring with you to our Educational Office" (Via Claudio 21, Building 6, 1st floor, Mon-Fri 09:30-13:00), which is the most concrete checklist STReGA publishes: 1. PASSPORT & VISA — "Bring with you your Passport and your Visa, we have to copy them"; 2. TAX CODE — "Don't forget your Tax Code (Codice Fiscale in italian). Bring with you the ORIGINAL DOCUMENT, NOT THE COPY"; 3. ENROLMENT — "We need your enrollment certificate with your matricula number. Remind: TO ENROL YOU MUST PRESENT THE DECLARATION OF VALUE TO THE SECRETARY OFFICE"; 4. QUESTURA — "Within 8 working days from your arrival in Italy, you must go to the 'QUESTURA' in order to complete the paperwork"; 5. PERMIT OF STAY — "Provide us a receipt's copy of the payment for the residence permit"; 6. BANK ACCOUNT — "Only if you have a scholarship, please provide us your italian bank account number and your address."

(6) FOR MATRICULATION AT THE STUDENT OFFICE generally: copy of passport; application form; passport photo; codice fiscale; residence permit or proof of having applied for it; Declaration of Value or ENIC-NARIC/CIMEA certificate; a EUR 16 duty stamp (marca da bollo) bought at a tabaccheria. SHORT ANSWER FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: this degree is close to free. NON-EU citizens are TOTALLY EXEMPT from the tuition contribution and pay only the regional right-to-study tax plus a EUR 16 stamp; EU non-Italian citizens pay a flat EUR 200 contribution plus the regional tax and stamp. Realistic 2026/27 totals: roughly EUR 167 per year for a non-EU student and roughly EUR 367 per year for an EU non-Italian student.

THE BINDING RULES (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27, "Esoneri parziali", verbatim): "e. STRANIERI (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono ESONERATI TOTALMENTE dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio secondo le disposizioni di cui al punto 1 sopra e l'imposta di bollo, entro il termine ordinario di scadenza per il versamento della I rata; f. EUROPEI (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un CONTRIBUTO FISSO PARI A 200 € per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 €. Se inferiore, possono effettuare l'iscrizione nella modalità ordinaria." The same guide confirms that for foreign-citizenship students "gli importi da pagare sono distinti solo in base alla cittadinanza (studenti comunitari oppure studenti extracomunitari)" — i.e. income assessment (ISEEU) is irrelevant to them.

REGIONAL RIGHT-TO-STUDY TAX 2026/27, three bands: EUR 130.00 (ISEEU up to 25,500); EUR 151.00 (ISEEU 25,500.01-51,000); EUR 173.00 (ISEEU above 51,000 or no ISEEU declaration). Stamp duty EUR 16.00. INSTALMENTS: 1st (60% + regional tax + stamp) by 2026-11-02; 2nd (20%) by 2027-03-01; 3rd (20%) by 2027-04-30. LATE SURCHARGES: EUR 50 up to 2027-01-15, EUR 110 from 2027-01-16, and EUR 100 from 2027-07-16 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments. "Nota: le date di scadenza possono essere soggette a variazioni" and refunds are possible "solo ed esclusivamente" where a statutory exemption applies — withdrawal from studies earns no refund.

FOR ITALIAN STUDENTS the ISEEU system applies instead: full exemption for first-year students with household ISEEU up to EUR 30,000; otherwise a fixed component of EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component up to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those filing no ISEEU declaration. Relevant merit reductions include a 50% cut for a first-year master's student who obtained the bachelor by 31 October of the third year with 110 cum laude.

[uncertain] THE REGIONAL-TAX FIGURE IS PUBLISHED INCONSISTENTLY ACROSS UNINA.IT. international.unina.it states a flat "€140/year regional tax" for both EU and non-EU students ("European students €200/year (tuition fees) + €140/year regional tax (compulsory) + €16.00 legal stamp (compulsory) – Non-european students €140/year regional fee (compulsory) + €16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)"), whereas the binding 2026/27 Guida gives the banded EUR 130 / 151 / 173. Since most international students file no Italian ISEEU declaration, the EUR 173 band is the prudent planning figure, and EUR 151 the likely one where a household-resident-abroad assessment is applied. BUDGET EUR 151-173, not EUR 140; the EUR 140 figure appears to be a stale carry-over. The tuition components themselves (EUR 200 for EU citizens, total exemption for non-EU citizens) agree across all sources and are not in doubt. Note also that the orientation portal for this course still links the PREVIOUS year's guide (guida_studente_rapida_25_26.pdf), so always open the current year's file from unina.it directly.

FUNDING SPECIFIC TO THIS DEGREE — genuinely worth knowing, and unusually generous relative to the fee level. The Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture runs its own scholarship scheme RESERVED TO INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: for a.y. 2025/2026 it offered "3 (three) scholarships, each with a duration of 2 years and a total amount of € 12,000.00" (EUR 6,000 gross per year). Eligibility is automatic — "The submission of an application for participation is not required" — for "All foreign students regularly registered on Universitaly by the deadline of May 31 and who have been previously admitted to the first year". Ranking is by CV (up to 23 points) and language certificates (up to 7), minimum score 16, ties resolved in favour of the younger candidate. Winners sign a contract at Via Claudio 21, Building 6, first floor, and must supply enrolment certificate, codice fiscale, IBAN/BIC/SWIFT, passport copy and a Declaration of Value or CIMEA equivalent. The scholarship is NOT cumulable with other UNINA awards for the same purpose but IS cumulable with ADiSURC regional grants and compatible with Erasmus+ and Erasmus Traineeship grants. OTHER FUNDING: ADiSURC regional right-to-study grants; the Double Degree pathway carries its own support — UniNa covers enrolment fees and provides mobility support up to the Erasmus+ study grant amount, with possible supplementary funding from MUR and DiSt.

IDENTITY AND CLASSIFICATION — Didactic Regulations in force from a.y. 2026/2027, Art. 1: "These Didactic Regulations govern the organisational aspects of the Master's Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering (class LM-23). The CdS in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering is hinged in Civil Engineering, Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture and is a course of study with an international character, as it also envisages a course of study entirely in English. Name of the course in English: Structural and Geotechnical Engineering | Class: LM-23 – Civil Engineering | Course language: Italian and English | Course delivery methods: conventional study course." Art. 2: "As can be seen from the extensive description above, THE COURSE OF STUDY IS NOT DIVIDED INTO SPECIFIC CURRICULA." Italian original (2024/25 regulations): "il corso di studi non è articolato in specifici curricula."

THE ENGLISH PATHWAY — Art. 2: "The Master Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering is international in character, in that it also provides a course of study entirely in English (Master Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering), which represents a different pathway for achieving the same specific educational objectives. This pathway is tabulated in the course regulations, so as to be clearly identifiable by the student, although it simply gathers together teachings that are substantially equivalent to those in Italian." And: "The English language pathway... aims to attract international students. This feature represents an important added value also for students of Italian nationality enrolled in this course, as they will be able to benefit from the advantages of their educational experience in a multi-cultural environment. The training offer in English is more oriented towards the training of an engineer destined to operate in a globalised market and ready to carry out his or her activity in international contexts." Italian original on the pairing mechanism: "il primo insegnamento obbligatorio... prevede l'alternativa fra un insegnamento in lingua italiana ed il corrispondente in lingua inglese"; and of sixteen Construction-Technique options for one slot, "cinque dei quali in lingua inglese".

BILINGUAL SELF-DESCRIPTION — orientamento.unina.it (Italian, updated a.a. 2026/2027): "La Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica (STReGA), incardinata nel Dipartimento di Strutture per l'ingegneria e l'Architettura (DIST), è un CORSO DI STUDI BILINGUE, offrendo anche un percorso formativo interamente in lingua inglese (MSc in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering)." English version: "The Master's Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering (STReGA), offered by the Department of Structures for Engineering and Architecture (DIST), is a bilingual program that also offers a track taught entirely in English (MSc in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering)." And: "Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica si articola in un curriculum o percorso formativo base ed in un percorso formativo con insegnamenti tutti in lingua inglese... È possibile inserire nel percorso formativo base anche insegnamenti in lingua inglese."

ADMISSION — Art. 4: "For enrolment in the Master's Degree Course in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering, in compliance with Art. 6 paragraph 2 of Italian Ministerial Decree 270/04..., specific access criteria are envisaged concerning the possession of curricular requirements (in terms of specific CFUs obtained in sets of SSDs) and the compulsory verification of the adequacy of the student's personal preparation." Art. 4 (Italian original): "Detti requisiti prevedono, tra l'altro, la documentata capacità di utilizzare fluentemente, in forma scritta e orale, la lingua inglese con riferimento anche ai lessici disciplinari." Art. 4.1: "The curricular requirements for admission are - as a rule - automatically possessed by graduates of the degree courses of class no. 8 in civil and environmental engineering pursuant to Ministerial Decree 509/99 and the degree courses of class L-7 in civil and environmental engineering pursuant to Ministerial Decree 270/04 who have followed the generalist or passing curriculum. Enrolment on the course is not permitted if more than 27 CFUs of the minimum curricular requirements specified in the following table are lacking." Art. 5: "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it." Italian original: "La verifica della personale preparazione è obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari."

MINIMUM CFU TABLE — 2026/2027 (new SSD codes): "MATH/02, MAT/03 — 18 | PHYS-01/03??? — 6 | CEAR-01/A, CEAR-01/B — 9 (*) | CEAR-03/A, CEAR-03/B — 9 | CEAR-05 — 9 (**) | MATH-04, CEAR-06 — 18 | CEAR-07 — 15 | CEAR-04, CEAR-08, CEAR-10 — 9". 2024/2025 version (old codes): "MAT/03, MAT/05 — 18 | FIS/01 — 6 | ICAR/01, ICAR/02 — 9 (*) | ICAR/04, ICAR/05 — 9 | ICAR/07 — 9 (**) | MAT/07, ICAR/08 — 18 | ICAR/09 — 15 | ICAR/06, ICAR/10, ICAR/17 — 9". Footnotes: "(*) Students who have already completed 6 CFU in SSD CEAR-01/A and CEAR-01/B can make up for it with a 3 CFU Supplementary Colloquium in SSD CEAR-01/A. (**) Students who have already completed 6 CFU in SSD CEAR-05 can make up for it with a 3 CFU Supplementary Colloquium in SSD CEAR-05."

CREDIT-GAP RULE — Art. 4.1: "Graduates who do not meet these requirements for an overall difference not exceeding 27 CFU will be allowed to propose, as part of the 120 CFU envisaged for the Master's degree, an educational pathway that envisages the passing of examinations of the degree course such as to compensate for the existing deficiencies highlighted by the failure to meet the minimums in the table." And: "Should these integrations correspond to a relatively limited number of credits (max 18 CFU), they will be agreed with the Study Plan Committee and included in the study plan that will provide more than 120 CFU for the Master's Degree. If, on the other hand, the additional integrations requested exceed the above-mentioned limit, the corresponding credits must necessarily be acquired prior to enrolment in the Master's Degree Course."

GRADE-AVERAGE GATE — Art. 4.2: "Verification of the fulfilment of the requirements relating to the student's personal preparation will be carried out, exclusively for students enrolled after 1 September 2011, on the basis of the average M of the marks (in thirtieths) obtained in the proficiency examinations for the degree, weighted on the basis of the relative consistencies in CFUs, as well as the duration of studies D1 expressed in course years, compared with the normal duration D2 of the course." AUTOMATIC ADMISSION CRITERIA table (2026/27): "D1=D2 → M≥21 | D1=D2+1 → M≥22.5 | D1≥D2+2 → M≥24". The 2024/25 Italian table adds a fourth column: "Studenti provenienti da altri Atenei — D1 qualunque — M≥24". And: "In the presence of applications for admission... from students who do not meet the criteria for automatic admission, the relevant Academic Coordination Committee examines the applications on the basis of the curriculum acquired and, in the event of a positive assessment, prepares supplementary assessment procedures to verify the personal preparation of these students. The assessment may provide for the identification of a training debt and the consequent allocation of an Additional Training Obligation (OFA)."

THE FORM A RULE — strega.unina.it Study plan page: "Those who, wishing to enroll in the Master's Degree in Structural and Geotechnical Engineering, show gaps in curricular requirements in SSD CFU and/or have an average rating lower than 24/30, before formalizing the enrollment must send a pre-evaluation request to the Teaching Office filling in the form A available in Forms section.
