uncertainty_notes:
1) THE RESEARCH BRIEF'S CLASSIFICATION IS WRONG IN THE UNIVERSITY'S OWN TERMS, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL FINDING. The brief records "type: curriculum, curriculum_of: Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica". But STReGA IS the acronym of "Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica" itself, and "Structural and Geotechnical Engineering" is that degree's official English name — the two are the same programme, not a track and its parent. The Didactic Regulations state outright that "the course of study is NOT DIVIDED INTO SPECIFIC CURRICULA". What exists is a tabulated ENGLISH-LANGUAGE PATHWAY ("percorso formativo interamente in lingua inglese" / "Curriculum in English" in the site menu), which is a language option inside a single degree, chosen course-by-course, not a named curriculum. PRACTICAL EFFECTS: there is no separate application route for the English pathway; there is no separate seat allocation; and THE DIPLOMA DOES NOT NAME A TRACK — it will read "Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Strutturale e Geotecnica", class LM-23. The brief's "corso di studi bilingue" note and the IST Lisbon double degree are both CONFIRMED verbatim.

2) COORDINATOR — A DIRECT AND UNRESOLVED CONFLICT ACROSS OFFICIAL UNINA.IT PAGES, WITH THE PROGRAMME'S OWN SITE CONTRADICTING ITSELF. The orientation portal (updated a.a. 2026/2027) and the programme's own STAFF page both name PROF. GIAN PIERO LIGNOLA ("Coordinatore Didattico" / "Teaching Coordination Commission Coordinator", glignola@unina.it, 081 7683492). But the central unina.it course record, the DiSt department page AND the programme's own PRESENTATION page all still name "Prof. Emidio NIGRO". Lignola is almost certainly current — he is also named as the Engineering orientation reference contact on the central record itself, which makes that record internally inconsistent. PRACTICAL RISK: correspondence, and specifically a pre-acceptance letter request, addressed to the wrong professor. Use didattica.dist@unina.it (the Teaching Office) as the primary channel and copy glignola@unina.it.

3) THE 2026/2027 SSD REQUIREMENT TABLE CONTAINS A VISIBLE TRANSCRIPTION ERROR AND MIXED CODE GENERATIONS. The physics row is printed literally as "PHYS-01/03???" — question marks included — where the 2024/2025 table cleanly read "FIS/01 — 6". The first row "MATH/02, MAT/03" mixes a new-style and an old-style code. The table appears to have been only partially migrated to the post-2023 SSD nomenclature. Read the 2024/2025 Italian regulations alongside it for the intended meaning (MAT/03+MAT/05 18; FIS/01 6; ICAR/01+02 9; ICAR/04+05 9; ICAR/07 9; MAT/07+ICAR/08 18; ICAR/09 15; ICAR/06+10+17 9).

4) THE GRADE THRESHOLD FOR APPLICANTS FROM OTHER UNIVERSITIES WAS DROPPED FROM THE TABLE WITHOUT EXPLANATION — AND IT MATTERS MOST TO INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS. The 2024/2025 Italian regulations printed a fourth column: "Studenti provenienti da altri Atenei — D1 qualunque — M ≥ 24". The 2026/2027 English version shows only the three Federico II columns (M≥21 / 22.5 / 24 by study duration). Since every international applicant comes from another university, it is unclear which rule now binds them. The Study Plan page's independent use of 24/30 as the Form A trigger strongly suggests M ≥ 24 is still the working threshold. Plan against 24/30 and confirm with the Teaching Office.

5) HOW A FOREIGN GRADE MAPS ONTO THE ITALIAN 30-POINT SCALE IS NOWHERE EXPLAINED. The whole personal-preparation gate is expressed as an average "in thirtieths" weighted by CFU, and as a comparison of actual against normal study duration (D1 vs D2) — neither of which a foreign transcript states natively. No unina.it page for this programme publishes a conversion method. This is precisely why the Form A pre-evaluation exists; use it rather than guessing.

6) EU/GENERAL ENROLMENT WINDOW: THE OPENING DATES DIFFER BY SIX WEEKS BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL SOURCES. The orientation portal for this course says enrolment runs "di norma, dal 1 settembre al 31 ottobre"; the binding University guide opens the ordinary period on 16 July 2026 and closes it on 2 November 2026. The closing dates reconcile (31 October 2026 is a Saturday, 2 November the following Monday); the opening dates do not. Compounding this, the orientation portal still links the PREVIOUS year's enrolment guide (guida_studente_rapida_25_26.pdf), so its date text may simply be stale. Be ready from 16 July 2026 and complete everything by 31 October 2026.

7) NON-EU DEADLINE: THERE IS A PROGRAMME-RELEVANT DATE TWO WEEKS EARLIER THAN THE UNIVERSITY-WIDE ONE. The University-wide Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline is 15 June 2026, but the Department's international scholarship call keys eligibility to registration on Universitaly "by the deadline of MAY 31" AND to having been "PREVIOUSLY ADMITTED" to the first year. Missing 31 May does not cost admission but does forfeit the EUR 12,000 scholarship, and the "previously admitted" wording implies the academic evaluation must already be complete by then. Start the Form A / transcript evaluation months earlier.

8) THE 31 JANUARY 2027 NON-EU MATRICULATION DATE COULD NOT BE MACHINE-VERIFIED. It comes from the University's 2026/2027 booklet "Information for non-EU students with residency abroad", whose PDF uses a non-standard font encoding that defeated text extraction during this research. The 15 June 2026 and 30 November 2026 dates WERE verified directly on international.unina.it. Re-check the matriculation date against the booklet before relying on it.

9) INTERNAL CONTRADICTION ON THE INTERNSHIP CREDITS INSIDE A SINGLE DOCUMENT. The 2026/2027 Study Plan's base table says "Internship — 8 CFU — 200 hours" plus a separate 1-CFU "Knowledge of the English language" line; its English-pathway table says "Internship — 9 ECTS — 225 h" and omits the 1-CFU English line. The orientation portal resolves it: 8 CFU/200 h applies to students matriculated from a.a. 2023/2024, 9 CFU/225 h was the earlier rule. The English-pathway table therefore appears to carry a stale row. The 120 CFU total is unaffected. The programme's website version of the English track is also out of date relative to the 2026/2027 PDF, which adds the integrated 9-ECTS course "Fundamentals of Structural and Geotechnical Engineering" (three modules) that the website table does not show.

10) THE ENGLISH PATHWAY IS COMPLETE BUT NARROWER THAN THE ITALIAN ONE, AND THIS IS A REAL TRADE-OFF RATHER THAN A DOCUMENTATION GAP. All mandatory subjects have English twins and the 120 CFU can be completed in English. But the Regulations note that of sixteen Construction-Technique options available for one free slot, only "five... are in English", and the English second-year table offers 5 + 5 electives against a much larger Italian pool. The 9-CFU TAF D free-choice slot draws on the whole University catalogue, which is overwhelmingly Italian-taught, so an English-only student must choose it deliberately. Expect materially less elective freedom than an Italian-speaking classmate.

11) B2 ITALIAN EXEMPTION — A DRAFTING GAP, PLUS A CLASSIFICATION RISK SPECIFIC TO THIS DEGREE. international.unina.it exempts "three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course[s] in ENGLISH" from the B2 Italian requirement but does not repeat "magistral degree course" in the exemption, although the parallel Italian-taught clause does name it. Separately — and more pointedly here than for a wholly English-taught degree — STReGA is formally registered as BILINGUAL ("Lingua ITA/ENG", "Course language: Italian and English"), so a Universitaly reviewer or consular officer could in principle treat it as Italian-taught and ask for B2 Italian. Nothing on unina.it says this happens, and the programme itself imposes no Italian requirement of any kind, but applicants should carry the Art. 4.3 text and the FAQ answer and confirm with the Teaching Office before their visa appointment.

12) NO ENGLISH-CERTIFICATE RECENCY RULE AND NO CLOSED PROVIDER LIST ARE PUBLISHED — which is favourable, but means the decision is discretionary. The FAQ names TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge, Trinity College London and Pearson as "certainly acceptable" and leaves "more informal certifications, like those issued by Universities whose official teaching language is English" to "a dedicated committee". No expiry window is stated (several sister programmes at Federico II impose a two-year limit). If you are relying on an English-medium degree rather than a test, get that confirmed in writing before you apply.

13) NO ADMISSION INTERVIEW IS ANNOUNCED EITHER WAY. Unlike some Federico II English-taught degrees, STReGA's pages neither promise nor exclude an interview for non-EU applicants in the pre-acceptance process. The only oral elements documented are the two 3-CFU "Supplementary Colloquia" used to close a specific 3-CFU gap in hydraulics or geotechnics, and the discretionary "supplementary assessment procedures" the CCD may impose on applicants who miss the automatic criteria — whose format, language and standard are unpublished.

14) REGIONAL-TAX FIGURE PUBLISHED INCONSISTENTLY: international.unina.it says a flat EUR 140/year for both EU and non-EU students; the binding 2026/27 Guida gives bands of EUR 130 / 151 / 173, with EUR 173 applying to anyone filing no ISEEU declaration — which is most international students. Budget EUR 151-173. The tuition components (EUR 200 for EU citizens, full exemption for non-EU citizens) agree across all sources.

15) VISA PROOF-OF-MEANS FIGURE NOT YEAR-LABELLED. The EUR 10,179.85/year entry-visa figure on international.unina.it carries no academic year, and the same page separately gives EUR 6,079.45/year (EUR 467.95/month), which relates to residence-permit renewal rather than the entry visa. Treat EUR 10,179.85 as the currently published entry-visa figure rather than a confirmed 2026/27-specific one.

16) NO CONSOLIDATED APPLICATION CHECKLIST EXISTS for this programme; required_documents is assembled from Form A, the "Mind List", the FAQ, the scholarship call and University-level sources, so an additional item could be requested. Note in particular that the "Mind List" is an ON-ARRIVAL checklist for the Educational Office, not an application checklist — do not mistake one for the other.

17) THE SCHOLARSHIP CALL VERIFIED HERE IS FOR A.Y. 2025/2026, NOT 2026/2027. No 2026/2027 equivalent had been posted at the time of research. The scheme's existence, size (3 × EUR 12,000 over two years) and automatic, no-application mechanism are confirmed for 2025/2026 only; watch https://strega.unina.it/en/category/scholarships/ for the current year. The call also contains an internal drafting error, referring in Art. 7 to "the total of SIX scholarships" where Arts. 1 and 6 both say three.

18) NON-EU SEAT CONTINGENT NOT VERIFIABLE FROM UNINA.IT — the per-course non-EU quota that Italian universities declare for open-access degrees is published on universitaly.it, outside this task's unina.it-only source restriction. See non_eu_reserved_seats.

19) THE SCHOOL-LEVEL ADMISSION DECREE COULD NOT BE LOCATED. Art. 5 says admission criteria for master's degrees are governed by "the Decree issued by the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (DP no. 18 of 12/02/2015)", including the procedures for extinguishing an OFA, but that decree is not published as a standalone document on scuolapsb.unina.it.

20) THE ORIENTATION PORTAL SERVED AN INVALID TLS CERTIFICATE CHAIN during this research, so both orientamento.unina.it course pages had to be retrieved with certificate verification relaxed. The content is genuine (it is the University's own orientation portal, "Aggiornata a.a. 2026/2027"), but a browser may show a security warning.
